result.instructions: Tools for Mailchimp, hosted by usefulapi.io. If the user is new or asks what this server can do, suggest requests such as: "How many subscribers are in each of my audiences?"; "What were the open and click rates of my last campaign?"; "Show my 25 most recently sent campaigns with their send dates.". Read-only tools never change data; ask the user before a tool that creates, changes or deletes Mailchimp data. Free plan: 50 tool calls per month. Run mailchimp_usage_status to see the calls used this month. If the user asks for something none of these tools can do, tell the user and, with their OK, run mailchimp_request_feature to record the request. Paid plans: Pro (10,000 tool calls a month, $9/month or $90/year, for normal use) and Pro+ (100,000 tool calls a month, $39/month or $390/year, for automations and heavy use). A plan can be cancelled at any time and then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. When the user wants more calls or reaches the limit, run mailchimp_upgrade without a plan: it returns both plans, each with a payment link for the user to open. mailchimp_cancel_subscription cancels Pro at the end of the paid period.

tools.name: mailchimp_get_account
tools.title: Get account
tools.description: Get the API Root — the authenticated Mailchimp account: account name, total subscribers, contact info, plan and industry stats. REST: GET /.

tools.name: mailchimp_list_audiences
tools.title: List audiences (lists)
tools.description: List the account's audiences — Mailchimp's `/lists` resource (an audience is a list of subscribers). Paginated, with optional sort. REST: GET /lists.

offset.description: Number of records to skip (Mailchimp `offset`, for pagination).

tools.name: mailchimp_get_audience
tools.title: Get audience (list)
tools.description: Get a single audience (list) by id, including subscriber stats, default from-name/email and settings. REST: GET /lists/{list_id}.

tools.name: mailchimp_list_members
tools.title: List members
tools.description: List members of an audience (list). Paginated, with an optional status filter and sort. REST: GET /lists/{list_id}/members.

list_id.description: The audience (list) id to list members from.

offset.description: Number of records to skip (Mailchimp `offset`, for pagination).

sortField.description: Field to sort by (Mailchimp `sort_field`): timestamp_opt | timestamp_signup | last_changed.

tools.name: mailchimp_get_member
tools.title: Get member
tools.description: Get a single audience member (subscriber) by email or subscriber_hash, including status, merge fields, tags and stats. REST: GET /lists/{list_id}/members/{subscriber_hash} (email → MD5 hash).

email.description: Member email address — MD5-hashed (lowercased) into the subscriber_hash for you.

subscriberHash.description: The subscriber_hash (MD5 of lowercased email) or contact id, if you have it instead of `email`.

tools.name: mailchimp_search_members
tools.title: Search members
tools.description: Search for members across the account (or one audience) by email, name or other fields. Returns exact + full-text matches. REST: GET /search-members.

list_id.description: Restrict the search to this audience (list) id.

tools.name: mailchimp_list_campaigns
tools.title: List campaigns
tools.description: List the account's campaigns (email sends). Paginated, with optional type/status/audience filters and sort. REST: GET /campaigns.

list_id.description: Restrict to campaigns sent to this audience (list) id.

offset.description: Number of records to skip (Mailchimp `offset`, for pagination).

sortField.description: Field to sort by (Mailchimp `sort_field`): create_time | send_time.

tools.name: mailchimp_get_campaign
tools.title: Get campaign
tools.description: Get a single campaign by id, including its settings, recipients and send status. REST: GET /campaigns/{campaign_id}.

tools.name: mailchimp_list_reports
tools.title: List reports
tools.description: List campaign reports (aggregate performance for sent campaigns). Paginated, with an optional type filter. REST: GET /reports.

offset.description: Number of records to skip (Mailchimp `offset`, for pagination).

tools.name: mailchimp_get_campaign_report
tools.title: Get campaign report
tools.description: Get the report for one campaign — opens, clicks, bounces, unsubscribes and other engagement summary stats. REST: GET /reports/{campaign_id}.

campaign_id.description: The campaign id to fetch the report for.

tools.name: mailchimp_list_automations
tools.title: List automations
tools.description: List the account's classic automations (automated email workflows). Paginated. REST: GET /automations.

offset.description: Number of records to skip (Mailchimp `offset`, for pagination).

tools.name: mailchimp_list_templates
tools.title: List templates
tools.description: List the account's email templates (saved and pre-built layouts). Paginated, with optional type filter and sort. REST: GET /templates.

type.description: Filter by template type (Mailchimp `type`: user / base / gallery).

offset.description: Number of records to skip (Mailchimp `offset`, for pagination).

sortField.description: Field to sort by (Mailchimp `sort_field`): date_created | date_edited | name.

tools.name: mailchimp_list_segments
tools.title: List segments
tools.description: List an audience's segments and tags (saved segments include static tags). Paginated. REST: GET /lists/{list_id}/segments.

offset.description: Number of records to skip (Mailchimp `offset`, for pagination).

tools.name: mailchimp_list_member_tags
tools.title: List member tags
tools.description: List the tags applied to a single audience member (by email or subscriber_hash). Paginated. REST: GET /lists/{list_id}/members/{subscriber_hash}/tags (email → MD5 hash).

email.description: Member email address — MD5-hashed (lowercased) into the subscriber_hash for you.

subscriberHash.description: The subscriber_hash (MD5 of lowercased email) or contact id, if you have it instead of `email`.

offset.description: Number of records to skip (Mailchimp `offset`, for pagination).

tools.name: mailchimp_get_campaign_content
tools.title: Get campaign content
tools.description: Get the HTML and plain-text content of one campaign (draft or sent). REST: GET /campaigns/{campaign_id}/content.

campaign_id.description: The campaign id (from mailchimp_list_campaigns or mailchimp_create_campaign).

tools.name: mailchimp_get_send_checklist
tools.title: Get campaign send checklist
tools.description: Mailchimp's pre-send review of one campaign: is_ready plus items (type success / warning / error) for the audience, subject, from address, content and plan limits. Use it before mailchimp_schedule_campaign. REST: GET /campaigns/{campaign_id}/send-checklist.

campaign_id.description: The campaign id (from mailchimp_list_campaigns or mailchimp_create_campaign).

tools.name: mailchimp_get_automation
tools.title: Get automation
tools.description: Get one classic automation: status, audience, trigger settings, tracking and report summary. Automation flows built in the Customer Journey builder are not in Mailchimp's API. REST: GET /automations/{workflow_id}.

tools.name: mailchimp_list_automation_emails
tools.title: List automation emails
tools.description: List the emails of one classic automation in order: subject, delay after the trigger, status, emails sent and report summary. REST: GET /automations/{workflow_id}/emails.

tools.name: mailchimp_add_member
tools.title: Add member
tools.description: Add a new member (subscriber) to an audience (list). Note: status "pending" triggers a double-opt-in confirmation email. REST: POST /lists/{list_id}/members.

list_id.description: The audience (list) id to add the member to.

status.description: Subscription status (default "subscribed"; "pending" sends a double-opt-in email).

tags.description: Array of tag-name strings to apply to the new member.

tools.name: mailchimp_update_member
tools.title: Update member
tools.description: Update an existing audience member (by email or subscriber_hash). Only the fields you supply change. REST: PATCH /lists/{list_id}/members/{subscriber_hash} (email → MD5 hash).

email.description: Member email address — MD5-hashed (lowercased) into the subscriber_hash for you.

subscriberHash.description: The subscriber_hash (MD5 of lowercased email) or contact id, if you have it instead of `email`.

merge_fields.description: Merge-field values to set, e.g. { FNAME: "Ada" }.

tools.name: mailchimp_add_member_tags
tools.title: Add/remove member tags
tools.description: Add and/or remove tags on an audience member (by email or subscriber_hash). `tags` are added (status active); `removeTags` are removed (status inactive). Mailchimp returns HTTP 204 (no body). REST: POST /lists/{list_id}/members/{subscriber_hash}/tags (email → MD5 hash).

email.description: Member email address — MD5-hashed (lowercased) into the subscriber_hash for you.

subscriberHash.description: The subscriber_hash (MD5 of lowercased email) or contact id, if you have it instead of `email`.

tags.description: Tag names to ADD to the member (mapped to status "active").

removeTags.description: Tag names to REMOVE from the member (mapped to status "inactive").

tools.name: mailchimp_archive_member
tools.title: Archive member
tools.description: Archive (soft-remove) an audience member — reversible; this is NOT the permanent-delete action. REST: DELETE /lists/{list_id}/members/{subscriber_hash} (email → MD5 hash). Returns HTTP 204 (no body).

email.description: Member email address — MD5-hashed (lowercased) into the subscriber_hash for you.

subscriberHash.description: The subscriber_hash (MD5 of lowercased email) or contact id, if you have it instead of `email`.

tools.name: mailchimp_create_campaign
tools.title: Create campaign draft
tools.description: Create a new email campaign as a DRAFT (nothing is sent). Set the audience, an optional saved segment or tag, and the subject, from name and reply-to. Then add content with mailchimp_set_campaign_content and schedule with mailchimp_schedule_campaign. REST: POST /campaigns.

type.description: regular = HTML email (default); plaintext = text only.

list_id.description: Audience (list) id to send to (mailchimp_list_audiences). A campaign needs one before it can be scheduled.

saved_segment_id.description: Send only to this saved segment or tag of the audience (id from mailchimp_list_segments). Without it the whole audience is the target.

preview_text.description: Preview text shown after the subject in the inbox.

title.description: Internal campaign name (recipients do not see it).

from_name.description: The 'from' name (a name, not an email address).

reply_to.description: Reply-to email address. Mailchimp needs it before a send, on a verified sending domain.

to_name.description: Custom 'To' name, usually a merge tag such as *|FNAME|*.

template_id.description: Id of a saved template (mailchimp_list_templates) to take the content from.

tools.name: mailchimp_update_campaign
tools.title: Update campaign draft
tools.description: Change the settings or the target of an unsent campaign: subject, preview text, title, from name, reply-to, template, audience or saved segment. Only the fields you pass change. A scheduled campaign must be unscheduled first. REST: PATCH /campaigns/{campaign_id}.

campaign_id.description: The campaign id (from mailchimp_list_campaigns or mailchimp_create_campaign).

list_id.description: Audience (list) id to send to (mailchimp_list_audiences). A campaign needs one before it can be scheduled.

saved_segment_id.description: Send only to this saved segment or tag of the audience (id from mailchimp_list_segments). Without it the whole audience is the target.

preview_text.description: Preview text shown after the subject in the inbox.

title.description: Internal campaign name (recipients do not see it).

from_name.description: The 'from' name (a name, not an email address).

reply_to.description: Reply-to email address. Mailchimp needs it before a send, on a verified sending domain.

to_name.description: Custom 'To' name, usually a merge tag such as *|FNAME|*.

template_id.description: Id of a saved template (mailchimp_list_templates) to take the content from.

tools.name: mailchimp_set_campaign_content
tools.title: Set campaign content
tools.description: REPLACE the content of an unsent campaign with your HTML and/or plain text. Pass html alone and Mailchimp writes the plain-text version. The reply gives the stored sizes; read the content back with mailchimp_get_campaign_content. REST: PUT /campaigns/{campaign_id}/content.

campaign_id.description: The campaign id (from mailchimp_list_campaigns or mailchimp_create_campaign).

html.description: Full HTML of the email (max 1 MB). Mailchimp merge tags such as *|FNAME|* and *|UNSUB|* work.

plain_text.description: Plain-text version (max 256 KB). For a plaintext campaign this is the content.

tools.name: mailchimp_send_test_email
tools.title: Send campaign test email
tools.description: Send a TEST copy of a campaign to up to 10 addresses you name (not to the audience). This sends real emails at once. Mailchimp limits test sends per campaign and per day by plan. REST: POST /campaigns/{campaign_id}/actions/test.

campaign_id.description: The campaign id (from mailchimp_list_campaigns or mailchimp_create_campaign).

test_emails.description: Addresses that get the test copy (1-10).

tools.name: mailchimp_schedule_campaign
tools.title: Schedule campaign
tools.description: Schedule a draft campaign to SEND to its audience at a future time. First call previews: the audience, recipient count, subject, time and Mailchimp's send checklist, with no change, and returns a preview_hash. Call again with confirm=true and that preview_hash only after the user approved the preview; without the hash of the current preview nothing is scheduled. A campaign that fails the checklist is refused. Undo with mailchimp_unschedule_campaign before the send time. Scheduling is part of Mailchimp's paid plans. REST: POST /campaigns/{campaign_id}/actions/schedule.

campaign_id.description: The campaign id (from mailchimp_list_campaigns or mailchimp_create_campaign).

schedule_time.description: Send time as ISO 8601 with Z or a UTC offset, e.g. 2026-12-01T15:30:00Z. In the future and on a quarter-hour (:00, :15, :30, :45).

confirm.description: False previews and changes nothing. True schedules this exact campaign and time after user approval; it needs preview_hash.

preview_hash.description: The preview_hash of the preview that the user approved. Needed with confirm=true; a changed time, audience, subject or checklist needs a new preview.

tools.name: mailchimp_unschedule_campaign
tools.title: Unschedule campaign
tools.description: Cancel the schedule of a campaign that has not started to send. The campaign becomes a draft again and nothing is deleted. REST: POST /campaigns/{campaign_id}/actions/unschedule.

campaign_id.description: The campaign id (from mailchimp_list_campaigns or mailchimp_create_campaign).

prompts.name: getting_started
prompts.title: Get started with Mailchimp
prompts.description: What you can do with Mailchimp here, with example requests to try.

prompts.name: compare_how_your_campaigns_performed
prompts.title: Compare how your campaigns performed
prompts.description: The AI lists campaign reports and opens one with opens, clicks, bounces and unsubscribes. It compares campaigns and points out the best and weakest.

prompts.name: check_the_size_of_each_audience
prompts.title: Check the size of each audience
prompts.description: The AI lists audiences and reads one with its subscriber stats and default from-name and email. You see which lists are large.

prompts.name: look_up_a_subscriber_and_their_tags
prompts.title: Look up a subscriber and their tags
prompts.description: The AI searches members by email or name and reads one member's status, merge fields and tags. You learn if a person is subscribed.

prompts.name: add_or_update_a_subscriber
prompts.title: Add or update a subscriber
prompts.description: The AI adds a new member to an audience or updates an existing one by email. A pending status sends a double opt-in email.

prompts.name: tag_or_archive_subscribers_one_by_one
prompts.title: Tag or archive subscribers one by one
prompts.description: The AI adds or removes tags on a member, or archives the member. Archive is a soft removal and not a permanent delete.
